decisions.reason: Because A is close to the core offer and was maintained on its own page in both 2023 and 2024, management is likely to continue it and justify weak visible results as normal long space-market sales cycles.
B has the strongest public validation through the ESA HERA mission and continued standalone presentation, so dropping it would be hard to justify after such visible commitment and success.
C was given its own page in both years and fits the firm's move toward advanced sensing, so management is likely to persist and treat any slow commercial traction as temporary.

D has weaker public commitment because it is only mentioned on the website, but its miniaturized LiDAR concept matches the announced strategic direction and space-qualification investment encourages continuation.
E is a recent launch in the firm's established camera domain and already received its own page, so management is likely to give it more time rather than write off the investment quickly.

F is the most vulnerable because it is only mentioned and serves a narrower niche, but as a very new product tied to strategic navigation and imaging capabilities management is still somewhat more likely to keep it than drop it.
